title: Composer, send, stop, approvals and reactions on Android (chat MVP)
description: Port Thread/Composer.swift with composer-keyboard.ts and composer-drafts.ts: send through bot-store.ts with optimistic local-* entries slotted by seq (bot-mirror.ts:179-201), stop, newSession, react, markRead, drafts per bot, keyboard avoidance, haptics (expo-haptics). Permission card (port PermissionCard.swift / PermissionCard.tsx): option kinds allow_once, allow_always, reject_once, reject_always -> respondPermission; cancelled and failed states; notices. Host methods: send, stop, newSession, respondPermission, react, markRead (HostClient.swift:199-250).
design: Every tap that shows or hides something animates (CLAUDE.md:25). Cross-client parity: the change summary must say which clients are affected and why (CLAUDE.md:44).
acceptance_criteria:
- from the Android phone, chat with a bot on a dev host and get a reply
- answer a permission request from the phone and see the tool run; stop mid-turn
- reactions and read markers show up on desktop and iPhone
- this closes the MVP: pairing, direct and relay transport, chat, approvals

title: Bot list and read-only thread on Android using the shared mirror
description: Wire HostClient + BotSync + BotMirror from the shared core to the channel transport: hello, sync, events with rev catch-up (since=rev; reset on hostId change; rev=0 when hello.rev < rev; resync = resubscribe; an undecodable event rewinds once to rev 0 and then shows update-app, never skipped: BotStore+Sync.swift:79-152, compatibility.md:41-52). Cache the mirror locally for instant launch (bot-mirror.ts storage injection). Screens: roster (bots and groups, status badges, unread, computer filter and ordering via computer-order.ts; port BotListView.swift), thread (port Thread/ChatRows.swift and TraceView.swift plus markdown-blocks.ts: kinds user/agent/thought/tool/plan/permission/notice; chat visibility isChat models.ts:196-207; replies RepliesView; jump to latest and reading position per ui-conventions.md "iOS jump to latest" and "Reading conversations"), details panel (DetailsPanel.tsx). Inverted FlatList or FlashList keyed by entry id.
design: Event stream starts with {"type":"hello",hostId,computerId,rev,usage,screen}, then bot and entry events sorted by rev, then live events; {"type":"resync"} under load (host/src/api/events.rs:55-93). Host methods: hello, sync, thread, history, botConversation, markRead (HostClient.swift:128-188). Measure catch-up: a 10k-entry history must land under 5 s on a mid-range phone; if the AEAD is the bottleneck, apply the native-binding upgrade path from the crypto slice.
acceptance_criteria:
- Android shows the same bots and messages as the iPhone and desktop for both hosts, including tool, plan and permission rows and markdown
- kill and relaunch restores from cache, then catches up by rev with no duplicates or gaps
- 10k-entry catch-up under 5 s on a mid-range phone (number recorded in the PR)

title: Android pairing UI: QR scan, deep link, stored computers, connection state
description: Port PairingView.swift, HostConnector.swift and the computers part of AccountStore.swift. QR with expo-camera CameraView onBarcodeScanned; deep links codync[-dev]://pair?... through expo-linking (intent filter comes from the scheme in app config). Keys in expo-secure-store (32-byte seeds only). Persist Computer {id,name,signKey,boxKey,urls,cloud,device} and the connection state per computer. Screens: welcome, pair, computers list with state connecting/online/offline/update-needed using BotSync.setConnection grace (bot-sync.ts:76-104). Compatibility card: app older than hello.minApp = update app; host version below the Android minHost (from the host slice) = update computer; unreadable version never blocks (compat.ts mirrors host/src/compat.rs, MIN_APP "2.3.0"). Build the shared Android chrome in apps/android/src/ui (sheet, ModalHeader, ScreenHeader, dialog, toggle) following docs/design/ui-conventions.md sections iPhone navigation, Shared application controls, Motion and status; use the .claude/skills/animate-expo and mobile-native skills for motion.
design: hello reply fields: hostId, computerId, signKey, boxKey, cloud, name, version, minApp, os, device, home, backends, rev, screen, analytics, urls (host/src/api/host.rs:59-80). Reset the mirror when hello.hostId changes. Unpair = forget the computer locally (revocation is loopback-only on the host: devices.rs:44-64). Android minHost = the host version that first accepts platform android.
acceptance_criteria:
- scan the QR from codync-host pair on a dev host: the computer appears online, survives app restart and host restart, reconnects with backoff
- a deep link opened from a browser or Notes pairs too
- the update-needed card shows against a host older than minHost
- also pairs with a main-environment host (scheme codync) using the main build

title: Channel transport and pairing in shared core, integration-tested against a real codync-host
description:
apps/shared/core/src/relay/{pairing,channel,transport}.ts implementing the HostTransport interface so HostClient and BotSync work unchanged.

Pairing URL codync[-dev]://pair?v=3&name&id&sk&bk&code&urls[&cloud] (host/src/service/mod.rs:268-285, Pairing.swift:39-58): v must be "3"; id must equal computerId(sk); sk = host Ed25519 public key, bk = host X25519 box key, both b64url; code = 16 random bytes b64url, not six digits (devices.rs:179); urls = direct http candidates (Tailscale first, then LAN); at least one of urls/cloud.

DeviceIdentity: one Ed25519 device key per account context plus one X25519 push key, seeds in injected secure storage. No separate device id; the host keys devices by dk.

Connection: race every direct URL ws://h:p/channel?v=1 (no bearer, http.rs:158-170), first handshake within 1.5 s wins, else relay wss://{cloud}/v1/relay/device/{computerId}?v=1[&pair=offerId] with a Codync-Sig header (ChannelTransport+Connection.swift:47-163). Handshake hello/welcome with 10 s timeouts; verify welcome.sig against the QR's sk, failure = identity changed, stop. Inner RPC {"id","m","b"} -> {"id","ok"} or {"id","err":{status,message}}; {"id","sub":"events"|"term","b"} -> {"id","ev"}... {"id","end":true}; {"id","cancel":true}; max 32 in flight and 4 subscriptions, reused id = 400 (channel.rs:39-40,439-542). Events body {since: rev, client: "android"}.

Keepalive: direct, host pings every 15 s, dead after 45 s silent; relay, send the text {"t":"ping"} every 30 s, dead after 75 s. Backoff 1 s doubling to 30 s with full jitter, reset after 60 s stable. Close codes: never retry 4001, 4003, 4410, 4400; reconnect immediately on 4100 and 4011 (rekey at 2^32 frames or 24 h); relay presence online:true means drop keys and re-hello; reject codes devices.rs:95-127; leaseExpired = retry.

Pairing exchange: hello.pair=true (relay adds &pair=offerId), first request {"id":1,"m":"pair","b":{code,name,platform:"android"}} (host checks the code, constant time, one use, 10 min TTL, 3 attempts per source per minute), reply {ok:{computerId,name}} then close 4100; verify computerId, reconnect normally, inner hello merges urls/cloud/name/boxKey/device into the stored Computer (ChannelTransport+Incoming.swift:199-221). Never use the cloud's boxKey for sealing (remote-relay.md:101). Mailbox mbox.* is optional in v1: skip.
design: Integration test in Node: spawn codync-host serve --bind 127.0.0.1 --port <random> with a temp CODYNC home, read <home>/token, call loopback POST /api/pairing (devices.rs:44-64) to mint the URL, pair with the TS client (needs the host from the android-platform slice), reconnect, hello, events subscription, createBot + send round trip, then revoke through loopback and expect close 4003 with no retry. Run it locally against the built host and in CI next to host.yml. React Native WebSocket takes custom headers as the third constructor argument (needed for Codync-Sig on the relay path); keep the WebSocket factory injectable so Node uses ws or the built-in client. Frames are text messages; max message 1 MiB (channel.rs:30).
acceptance_criteria:
- integration test green against a locally built host (direct path), repeatable in CI
- a Node script pairs with a locally running dev host and codync-host devices lists platform android
- revoking the device closes the channel with 4003 and the client stops retrying
- relay path verified against the cloud URL from the QR

title: Scaffold apps/android: Expo dev-client app with dev and main environments
description: Create apps/android with create-expo-app on the current SDK (docs on 2026-10-13 list SDK 57 / RN 0.86): TypeScript strict, Expo Router, New Architecture, expo-dev-client from day one (WebRTC, speech recognition, widgets never run in Expo Go). app.config.ts reads CODYNC_ENV=dev|main and apps/shared/Config/{env}.plist the way apps/desktop/tools/account-config.mjs does: name "Codync Dev"/"Codync", android package com.pokai.codync.android with a .dev suffix for dev, scheme codync-dev / codync (host/src/environment.rs:80-83), cloudURL, version = MARKETING_VERSION. Metro watchFolders ../shared/core and tsconfig paths @core/*. Polyfill crypto.getRandomValues with expo-crypto. Baseline deps: expo-secure-store, expo-camera, expo-linking, expo-crypto, @noble/curves, @noble/ciphers, @noble/hashes. Scripts: typecheck, test (node --test), android:dev = CODYNC_ENV=dev npx expo run:android. Prerequisites on a Mac: Android Studio or command-line tools, JDK 17, adb, an emulator or a USB phone.
design: Prefer config plugins over committing the generated android/ directory; gitignore prebuild output. Both env variants must install side by side on one phone (different package ids and schemes), mirroring the iOS Dev app isolation in docs/guides/dev-app.md. Add the apps/android line to docs/architecture/file-structure.md. Keep the first screen a placeholder; pairing UI is the next slice.
acceptance_criteria:
- CODYNC_ENV=dev npx expo run:android installs and launches on an emulator or phone; main variant installs next to it
- npm run typecheck green; a trivial core import compiles through @core/*
- adb devices shows the target; toolchain steps written into docs/guides/development.md
- patch version bump at merge; commit feat(android): scaffold Expo app
notes: Needs JDK 17, ANDROID_HOME pointing at an Android SDK with cmdline-tools and an API 34+ system image, adb, and an emulator or a USB phone with debugging enabled.

title: Host: accept platform android when pairing and count it as a phone for push muting
description: pair rejects any platform other than ios or macos with a 400 and close 4002 (host/src/remote/channel.rs:567-569). Accept "android". The events subscription counts client=="ios" to hold pushes while a phone is connected (host/src/api/events.rs:36-45,81; hub.rs:63,519 ios_connected; push.rs:110): rename to phone clients and include "android" so Android pushes (later) are also muted while the app is connected. Leave update/install.rs:128 (App Store gating) alone. Grep host/src for other "ios"/"macos" platform matches and decide each. Update compatibility.md (platform strings) and remote-relay.md (pair body).
design: Existing pair tests live at channel.rs:720-919; add one pairing with platform android and one checking the events guard with client "android". Device struct stores platform as a string (host/src/store/devices.rs:31-42), no enum to extend. Protocol addition, so a minor version bump; record the resulting version in the Android app as minHost (iOS uses "2.12.0", apps/ios/Kit/Sources/CodyncKit/Models/Compatibility.swift:14).
acceptance_criteria:
- cargo test green with the new tests
- a device paired with platform android appears in codync-host devices
- version bump minor (build: bump version to X.Y.Z) and commit feat(host): accept android devices
- the bumped version is written into the Android plan as minHost

title: Implement the E2E channel crypto in TypeScript against the shared vectors
description: apps/shared/core/src/relay/crypto.ts: computerId, handshake (hello/welcome signatures, transcript hash, X25519 + HKDF-SHA256 directional keys), frame seal/open with chunking, offerId, SAS, Codync-Sig request signature, sealed-box open (push and mailbox payloads). Pure JS: @noble/curves (ed25519, x25519), @noble/ciphers (chacha20poly1305 IETF), @noble/hashes (sha256, hkdf), crypto.getRandomValues (expo-crypto polyfill on the phone). The test loads docs/reference/fixtures/remote-relay-vectors.json and checks every vector, like host/src/remote/crypto.rs (include_str!) and apps/ios/Kit/Tests/CodyncKitTests/RelayVectorsTests.swift. Do not change the vectors.
design:
From host/src/remote/crypto.rs. computerId = b64url(SHA-256(sk)[0..16]) (:60-68). hello.sig = Ed25519_dk("codync/hs1/v1" || cidRaw || dk || ekD || n32) and welcome.sig = Ed25519_host(TH) with TH = SHA-256("codync/hs2/v1" || cidRaw || dk || ekD || n || ekH) (:104-126). ss = X25519(ekD, ekH), reject all-zero. prk = HKDF-Extract(salt=TH, ikm=ss); kD2H = Expand(prk, "codync/d2h/v1", 32); kH2D = Expand(prk, "codync/h2d/v1", 32). Frame {"t":"f","c":u64,"d":b64url(ct||tag)}: nonce = 4 zero bytes || u64_be(c), aad = "codync/frame/v1" || u64_be(c), plaintext = flag (0x00 last, 0x01 more) || chunk <= 256 KiB (:130-159); counters strictly consecutive per direction, mismatch closes 4002 (:218-234); reassembly caps 1 MiB device->host, 16 MiB host->device. offerId = b64url(SHA-256("codync/offer/v1" || codeBytes)[0..16]) (:292). SAS = u32_be(SHA-256("codync/sas/v2" || hostSignPub || dk || nD || nH)[0..4]) mod 10^6, zero-padded (:285-289). Codync-Sig header v=1,kid=dk,ts=ms,nonce=16B b64url,sig over "codync-sig-v1
METHOD
host[:port]
path?query
ts
nonce
b64url(SHA-256(body))" (:301-316). Sealed box :240-276, fresh epk per seal. Labels are raw ASCII without NUL. Host verifies device signatures with verify_strict (:72), so produce canonical RFC 8032 signatures.
acceptance_criteria:
- every vector in remote-relay-vectors.json passes under node --test
- a benchmark note in the PR: seal+open of 16 MiB in Node and on a mid-range Android phone under Hermes; ceiling: below 2 MB/s on device means swap the AEAD to react-native-quick-crypto or react-native-libsodium behind the same interface
- cmp against the Python generator per docs/reference/fixtures/README.md still matches (no vector changes)

title: Extract framework-free core from apps/desktop into apps/shared/core
description:
Move the pure TypeScript the Android app needs out of the Electron renderer so both clients share one implementation.

Move (with their *.test.ts): src/shared/{models,compat,mirror-window,composer-drafts,files}.ts; src/renderer/client/host-client.ts (HostClient, HostTransport, parseEvent, base64 helpers; LoopbackTransport stays in desktop); src/renderer/store/{bot-store,bot-sync,bot-mirror,memory-store,file-downloads,cloud,computer-order}.ts with storage and bridge injected instead of localStorage / window.codync; src/renderer/lib/{observable (class only; the useSyncExternalStore hook stays in desktop),computer-roster,message-preview,star-ask}.ts; src/renderer/views/thread/{bot-exchange,markdown-blocks,composer-keyboard}.ts.

Leave in desktop: prefs.ts (storage event), environment.ts, ssh*.ts, computer-access.ts, theme.ts, slide.ts, fonts.ts.
design: Desktop tsconfig already maps @shared/* (apps/desktop/tsconfig.json:17); add @core/* -> ../shared/core/src/* there and in electron-vite resolve.alias. Core has zero runtime deps: no react, electron, window, localStorage, document. bot-mirror.ts currently reads window.codync.appVersion and localStorage: inject both. Keep the node runner (package.json:19 node --test --experimental-strip-types) and add the core glob. Only erasable TS syntax (no enums, namespaces, decorators, parameter properties) so Node strip-types and Metro both load the files unchanged. Add a test that greps core for forbidden imports/globals. Wire model notes: entry kinds user/agent/thought/tool/plan/permission/notice (models.ts:181-193), isChat rule models.ts:196-207, rev upsert bot-mirror.ts:179-201, reconnect/catch-up bot-sync.ts:107-158,231-244.
acceptance_criteria:
- apps/desktop: npm run typecheck, npm test, npm run build green
- node --test --experimental-strip-types over apps/shared/core green, including the forbidden-import test
- desktop behaviour unchanged: chat through CODYNC_PORT=19223 npm run dev
- patch version bump; commit refactor(desktop): extract shared core

title: Port the Codync iPhone app to Android with Expo
description:
Goal: an installable Android APK (Expo/React Native, dev client) that pairs with a codync-host by QR or deep link, connects directly or through the Cloudflare relay over the E2E channel, and does chat: bot list, thread, composer, approvals, attachments. Then push, account sign-in, the RPC screens, terminal, remote screen, voice.

Plan document: docs/archive/android-expo-port-plan-2026-10-13.md (architecture, server changes, library choices, risks).

Sizes: iOS app 183 Swift files / 28,312 LOC. Reusable desktop TypeScript ~2.5k LOC (models, compat, mirror-window, host-client, bot-store, bot-sync, bot-mirror, memory-store, markdown-blocks, bot-exchange).

Layout: apps/android/ (Expo app: Expo Router, strict TS, dev client, never Expo Go) and apps/shared/core/ (framework-free TS shared by desktop and Android through a tsconfig path alias, no npm workspace).

Server changes that block Android: pair platform gate host/src/remote/channel.rs:567-569; push-mute guard client=="ios" host/src/api/events.rs:81 + hub.rs:519 + push.rs:110; cloud device enum cloud/src/routes/account.ts:61; relay is APNs-only relay/src/index.ts:29,76-110.

Skip: Live Activity (no Android analog), computer use (byproduct of chat + remote screen), Sign in with Apple.

Rules: every merge under apps/ or host/ bumps MARKETING_VERSION, host/Cargo.toml and apps/desktop/package.json (+ apps/android/app.json once it exists); the Android version must equal the shared version so hello.minApp works; Android minHost = the first host version that accepts platform "android". Conventional commits; several agents share dev.

MVP = children .1 to .8, about 10 working days. Parity minus the skips about 28 days.
notes: Plan: docs/archive/android-expo-port-plan-2026-10-13.md. Research grounded in docs/reference/remote-relay.md, docs/reference/compatibility.md, host/src/remote/{channel,crypto,push}.rs, cloud/src/routes/account.ts, relay/src/index.ts, apps/desktop/src/{shared,renderer/store,renderer/client}, apps/ios/Kit. Expo library facts checked 2026-10-13 (SDK 57 / RN 0.86 current).

title: Release pipeline, versioning and docs for the Android app
description: CI: apps/android typecheck and core tests on PRs; on v* tags build a sideloadable APK (expo prebuild then ./gradlew assembleRelease on ubuntu with JDK 17 and the Android SDK, keystore from secrets; or eas build -p android --profile preview with buildType apk) and attach it to the GitHub release next to the desktop artifacts (mirror .github/workflows/release-desktop.yml). Play Store AAB later. Versioning: extend the bump procedure (CLAUDE.md:75-77) with apps/android/app.json version and versionCode; the Android version must equal MARKETING_VERSION so hello.minApp comparisons hold. Docs: file-structure.md (apps/android, apps/shared/core), compatibility.md (platform string android, Android minHost), development.md (Android build and run), ui-conventions.md (Android section), docs/README index. The update-needed card links to the GitHub release APK.
design: Hosts hold releases that raise minApp until the App Store has the iPhone app (CLAUDE.md:74); Android has no store gate, the APK ships with the release. Sideloading only needs a consistent signing key across releases so updates install over the previous version.
acceptance_criteria:
- a tag produces a signed APK that installs over the previous version on a phone
- docs updated and linked from docs/README.md
- one version bump per merge, Android included

title: Settings, bot and group editors, memory, usage, routines and marketplace on Android
description: The remaining RPC-backed screens, ported from apps/ios/Views and CodyncUI, one PR per group with a version bump each: Settings (name, analytics opt-in for PostHog with the same event names and no SDK, docs/features/analytics.md:39-44); BotEditorView and GroupEditorView (createBot, updateBot, deleteBot, reorderBots, agentModels picker, backends from hello.backends, listDirs); Memory views (memory-store.ts); UsageView (usage); Routines (RoutinesView, RoutineEditorView, RoutineWebhookPanel; phone parts of docs/features/routines.md); Marketplace (MarketplaceView, InstalledView, AgentSheet, ConnectorSignInFlow, ComposioViews: refreshBackends, agentAuth, agentAuthenticate, setAgentEnv; Composio OAuth through expo-web-browser) without the setup terminal, which is its own slice.
design: Host method list: HostClient.swift:128-353. Menus follow the platform (CLAUDE.md:25 for iOS: menus are always the system ones); on Android use Material menus and bottom sheets, never hand-built dropdowns. Views hold no I/O (clean-code.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- each screen reaches parity with the iPhone against the same host
- every host method in HostClient.swift except term*, screen* and registerActivity is exercised from Android at least once
- one PR per screen group, each with a version bump

title: Account sign-in and cloud computers on Android: Clerk, access requests, SAS
description: Port AccountSession.swift, CloudClient.swift and AccessRequestView.swift. Sign in with @clerk/clerk-expo (Google; Sign in with Apple is skipped). The cloud JWT must carry sid and iss equal to CLERK_ISSUER (cloud/src/auth.ts:127); CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES may need the Android app, unverified. POST /v1/devices {name, platform} with Codync-Sig: the enum is ios|macos|linux|windows (cloud/src/routes/account.ts:61), add android (cloud change, no version bump). GET /v1/computers -> access none|pending|granted. Access request: commit = b64url(SHA-256("codync/sascommit/v1" || dk || nD)) with nD 32 random bytes kept in memory; poll GET /v1/access-requests/{id} every 2 s until hostNonce; POST .../reveal {nonce}; show the 6-digit SAS; poll until approved; connect over the relay and pin boxKey from the inner hello; DELETE to cancel. Account devices hold a 15-minute lease, leaseExpired means retry (CloudClient.swift:55-130, host/src/remote/cloud.rs:333-552, remote-relay.md:478-479). Account switcher and sign-out (unregister push, drop the account-scoped device key).
design: Relay admission: 403 if dk is blocked or not in the ACL (iOS retries 403 three times), 404 unknownComputer, 429 above 16 sockets, 426 wrong v (cloud/src/relay.ts). Hosts in Approval::Auto approve without the human comparison (cloud.rs:333-343); the normal path is codync-host access approve after comparing the code.
acceptance_criteria:
- sign in on Android, see the account's computers, request access, approve on the computer after comparing the code, chat over the relay with no QR
- revoke from the computer: the app shows revoked and stops retrying
- the Clerk authorized-parties question is resolved and documented

title: Push notifications for Android: FCM path in relay, host and app
description:
Today the relay is APNs-only (relay/src/index.ts:29 BUNDLE_ID, 76-80 apnsTopic, 101-110 register with a hex APNs token, 219+ pushBatch) and the host push body is APNs-shaped (host/src/remote/push.rs:146-156).

Relay: POST /register {platform:"android", token:<fcm>, env, kind:"alert"} -> ticket carrying the platform; FCM HTTP v1 sender (service-account JWT signed with Web Crypto RS256, Workers-compatible); data-only high-priority message carrying the same sealed payload fields. Host: platform-neutral alert fields next to the APNs ones, keep sealing through crypto.rs:267-276; push muting while a phone is connected comes from the android-platform slice. App: expo-notifications with google-services.json via EAS or FCM credentials; Android 13+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS (call setNotificationChannelAsync before requesting a token); FCM token -> relay ticket -> registerDevice {ticket, relay, pushKey, ctx, name} (host/src/api/remote.rs:16-28); a background task (expo-task-manager or Notifee) opens the sealed payload with the X25519 push key from secure store and posts a local notification with bot name and avatar; unregisterDevice on unpair and sign-out. Alert kinds needs-you, done, failed (docs/design/push-and-live-activity.md). No Live Activity: skip registerActivity.
design: Data-only FCM runs the JS task even when the app is killed on Android, but Doze and OEM battery managers can delay it; accept and document. Relay changes do not bump the version; host changes bump minor. Keep iOS behaviour byte-identical: the APNs path stays as is, the Android path is additive.
acceptance_criteria:
- with the app in background and when killed, a bot reply produces a notification with decrypted title and body on Android
- no notification while the app is connected
- relay tests cover platform android; iPhone push regression-checked

title: Attachments on Android: chunked upload, download and share
description: Port Attachments.swift, ComposerAttachment.swift, FileDownloadCard.swift and FileDownload.swift. Pick images and files (expo-image-picker, expo-document-picker); upload in 384 KiB chunks upload {botId, uploadId, name, offset, data, done} then send {attachments:[uploadId]}; download through readUpload {botId, uploadId, offset} and bot-generated files through readFile {entryId, fileId, offset} using file-downloads.ts with an expo-file-system sink; share with expo-sharing; inline image preview. Limits: 100 MB user uploads, 100 MiB bot files. Attachments bypass the offline mailbox, so queue them client-side (docs/features/file-attachments.md:13-59).
design: Keep each request under the 1 MiB device-to-host reassembly cap (the frame layer chunks at 256 KiB). HEIC is not an Android concern; still downscale very large images before upload as iOS does. Progress and cancel per upload.
acceptance_criteria:
- send a photo and a PDF from Android; the desktop shows the same attachments
- receive a bot-generated file and open it in another app via share
- progress and cancel work; a cancelled upload leaves no orphan on the host

title: Android home-screen widget (optional)
description: Port the apps/ios/Widgets usage and bot widget with react-native-android-widget (config plugin, dev client). It reads the cached mirror the app already stores (bot list, unread, usage); tapping opens the bot through the deep link. Periodic refresh only (Headless JS capped at 30 s, minimum 30-minute interval). No Live Activity analog: skip ActivityKit parity (docs/design/mobile-widgets.md).
design: Zero host or relay impact; pure client chrome on data the app already fetches.
acceptance_criteria: - the widget shows bots, unread and usage from the last sync and opens the right thread

title: Voice on Android: dictation and TTS engine, then realtime calls
description: Port CodyncUI/Call (CallView, CallOperator and the engines). Part 1, on-device: expo-speech-recognition for STT (dev client; continuous mode needs API 33+) feeding an ordinary send, expo-speech for TTS of final replies, the same call-bar UX (docs/features/voice-call.md:18-33). Part 2, realtime: voiceSession {provider, model, voice} mints short-lived credentials from the host vault; OpenAI realtime over WebRTC with react-native-webrtc owning mic capture and routing (do not also open the mic with expo-audio), Gemini over WebSocket; barge-in; voiceStatus, setVoiceKey, voiceModels, voiceTranscribe, voiceSpeak (voice-call.md:139-148).
design: The host never sees audio, only text (CLAUDE.md:35). Background playback needs a foreground service or ongoing notification on Android.
acceptance_criteria:
- dictate a message and hear the reply on Android
- realtime call with OpenAI and Gemini keys stored in the host vault
- audio keeps playing with the screen off

title: Remote screen viewer on Android with react-native-webrtc
description: Port CodyncUI/Screen (ScreenView, ScreenCanvas, ScreenSession). screenStatus; screenPrepare {relay} (the host signs POST /v1/host/screen-ice for Cloudflare TURN credentials); screenOffer {session, sdp, display?} with a non-trickle SDP offer; screenClose; screenTakeover. Video H.264; data channels input (reliable) and input-fast (unordered pointer moves); touch to pointer mapping, pinch and zoom, orientation; takeover semantics (bots are look-only while the phone holds the session) (docs/features/remote-screen.md:7-35, host/src/screen/). Libraries: react-native-webrtc with @config-plugins/react-native-webrtc pinned to the Expo SDK major.
design: A plugin version that does not match the Expo SDK breaks the build. Android defaults to software codecs since 2023; opt into hardware H.264 through WebRTCModuleOptions and measure. The protocol is platform-neutral; no host or relay change.
acceptance_criteria:
- view and control the computer from Android over LAN and over the relay
- 1080p at 20 fps or better on a mid-range phone with hardware decode; input latency under 150 ms on LAN
- releasing takeover restores bot control

title: Agent setup terminal on Android: xterm.js in a WebView over the term subscription
description: Port Marketplace/SetupTerminal.swift (SwiftTerm). agentSetup {backend, step: install|login, method?, cols, rows} -> {term}; subscribe {"sub":"term","b":{term}} over the channel (channel.rs:507-513; the loopback SSE route /term/{id} is not reachable from phones, http.rs:172-185); stream {"type":"output","data":<padded base64>} then {"type":"exit","code"} then end, scrollback replayed first (host/src/agent/term.rs:46-77); input termInput {term, data: padded base64}, termResize {term, cols, rows}, termClose {term} (host/src/api/host.rs:96-123). Renderer: xterm.js inside react-native-webview (for example @fressh/react-native-xtermjs-webview).
design: Known Android bug: xterm.js in a WebView buffers soft-keyboard input until a double Enter (xterm.js issue 5108); add a plain text input row as a fallback. Only used for installing and signing in to a coding-agent backend, not general terminal access.
acceptance_criteria:
- install and sign in to a coding agent backend from Android end to end
- resize on rotation; closing the sheet closes the term
